body.en:
• Radian vs. Degree Mode: ACT problems frequently alternate between degrees and radians. Always verify your calculator status line before evaluating trig functions, especially when finding angles or amplitudes.
  • Pythagorean Identity Variations: \( \sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1 \) is the most tested trig identity on the ACT. Look for algebraic rearrangements such as \( 1 - \sin^2\theta = \cos^2\theta \) and \( \frac{\sin^2\theta}{1 - \cos\theta} = 1 + \cos\theta \).
  • ASTC Quadrant Signs: Remember 'All Students Take Calculus': Quadrant I (All positive), Quadrant II (Sine positive), Quadrant III (Tangent positive), Quadrant IV (Cosine positive). A common error is missing the negative sign when given \( \theta \) in Quadrants II or III.
  • Period of a Sinusoid: For \( y = A \sin(Bx) \) or \( y = A \cos(Bx) \), the period is \( \frac{2\pi}{B} \) (or \( \frac{360^\circ}{B} \)), NOT \( 2\pi B \). Amplitude is \( |A| \), and the vertical midline is \( y = D \).
A right triangle has opposite \( 3 \) and hypotenuse \( 5 \). Find \( \sin\theta \). \[ \sin\theta=\tfrac{3}{5}. \]

question.en: In right triangle \(ABC\) with \(C = 90°\), \(a = 5\), \(c = 13\). Find \(\sin A\), \(\cos A\), \(\tan A\).
If \(\cos\theta = -\frac{4}{5}\) and \(\theta\) lies in Quadrant II, what is the value of \(\tan\theta\)?

solution.en: In Quadrant II, \(x = -4\) and \(r = 5\). Using \(x^2 + y^2 = r^2\), we have \((-4)^2 + y^2 = 5^2 \Rightarrow 16 + y^2 = 25 \Rightarrow y = 3\) (since sine is positive in Quadrant II). Therefore, \(\tan\theta = \frac{y}{x} = -\frac{3}{4}\).

question.en: What is the period of the trigonometric function \(f(x) = 4\sin(3x) - 2\)?

solution.en: For any sinusoidal function of the form \(f(x) = A\sin(Bx - C) + D\), the period is given by \(\frac{2\pi}{B}\). Here \(B = 3\), so the period is \(\frac{2\pi}{3}\).
